title: Minimum Cost Homecoming of Robot

monster.name: Pathway Sentinel
monster.title: Surveyor of Coordinate Tolls
monster.defeatQuote: Cost independent of path geometry computed along monotonic axis lines!

description: A robot starts at `startPos = [startRow, startCol]` and must reach `homePos = [homeRow, homeCol]`. Traveling into row r costs `rowCosts[r]`, into col c costs `colCosts[c]`. Return the minimum cost to reach home.
starterCode:
def minCost(startPos: list[int], homePos: list[int], rowCosts: list[int], colCosts: list[int]) -> int:
    pass
solutionCode:
def minCost(startPos: list[int], homePos: list[int], rowCosts: list[int], colCosts: list[int]) -> int:
    r1, c1 = startPos
    r2, c2 = homePos
    ans = 0
    step_r = 1 if r2 >= r1 else -1
    for r in range(r1 + step_r, r2 + step_r, step_r):
        ans += rowCosts[r]
    step_c = 1 if c2 >= c1 else -1
    for c in range(c1 + step_c, c2 + step_c, step_c):
        ans += colCosts[c]
    return ans
hints: Because costs are non-negative, any monotonic Manhattan path pays exactly for every intermediate row and column.
